category_title: Students with learning/speech disabilities who are on-task during active music-making but off-task during noninstructional transitions
minimal_context: The student is assigned to complete a music worksheet individually during Session 1 of a third-grade class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time to complete your music worksheet individually.

STUDENT: (Leans over to the next desk) Hey, do you know the answer to this first one?

TUTOR: Try your best on your own.

STUDENT: (Continues talking to the classmate) I think it's a quarter note, right?

TUTOR: Please keep working.

STUDENT: (Ignores the worksheet completely and continues the unassigned peer interaction) Anyway, what are you doing after school today?

options.A: Review antecedent data to create a hypothesis statement that includes the perceived reason for the behavior.
options.B: Purposefully plan opportunities for the student to interact both formally and informally during music classes.
options.C: Require the student to present to the class and engage in discourse about the worksheet until satisfied.
options.D: Ask the student what they think went wrong on the worksheet instead of telling them what went wrong.
